column2: 由 stock（此处指套在腿上的筒状物）＋ -ing 构成；stock 一支 ← 古英语 stocc（树干、桩）← 原始日耳曼语 *stukkaz
column3: a close-fitting covering for the foot and leg, worn under clothes
column5: She tore a stocking on the chair leg.|He hung a stocking by the fireplace.
column6: a soft tube pulled up over the leg – 套在腿上的一截软筒
column7: 长筒袜：从脚一直套到膝上的那种|丝袜：同一形制，用极薄的料子织成

column2: 中古英语 stomak ← 古法语 estomac ← 拉丁语 stomachus ← 希腊语 stomachos（食道、口部）← stoma（口）
column3: the organ inside the body where food is broken down after being swallowed
column5: He complained of pain in his stomach.|I cannot stomach his rudeness any longer.
column6: the pouch where swallowed food is broken down – 咽下去的东西在这个囊里被化开
column7: 胃：食物进去后被化开的那个器官|胃部：连着周围一片说，指位置|忍受：把「能装得下、化得开」用到难堪之事上

column2: 中古英语 ston ← 古英语 stān ← 原始日耳曼语 *stainaz（石）← 原始印欧语 *steyh₂-（变硬）
column3: a hard solid piece of rock
column5: He threw a stone into the pond.|The ring holds a deep green stone.
column6: a hard lump that keeps its shape under force – 受力也不变形的硬块
column7: 石头：山石水石那种硬块|宝石：切磨过的硬块，看重的是色与光|果核：果肉中间那块硬的，硬度上与石相类

column2: 中古英语 stool ← 古英语 stōl（椅、座）← 原始日耳曼语 *stōlaz（椅）← 原始印欧语 *steh₂-（站立）
column3: a seat with legs but no back or arms
column5: He sat on a stool at the bar.|Pull up a stool and join us.
column6: a seat that holds you up and nothing more – 只托住人、别的都不给的座位
column7: 凳子：有腿无靠背的座位|矮凳：同类中矮的那种，多供垫脚或矮坐

column2: 中古英语 stoupen ← 古英语 stūpian（俯身、弯下）← 原始日耳曼语 *stūpōną ← 原始印欧语 *(s)tewb-（顶、撞）
column3: to bend the upper body forward and down
column5: She stooped to pick up the coin.|He would never stoop to cheating.
column6: to bring the upper body down toward the ground – 把上身朝地面压下去
column7: 弯身：腰背向前下方折|俯身：同一动作，多为看清或取物|屈就：把身子放低这层用到身份上，指自降身份（同形的「门廊」是另一支，借自荷兰语，与此无关）

column2: 中古英语 stoppen ← 古英语 stoppian（塞住、堵住）← 原始日耳曼语 *stuppōną（塞住）← 原始印欧语 *(s)tewp-（顶、塞）
column3: to no longer move or continue
column5: The bus stopped at the corner.|Nothing could stop him from trying again.
column6: to bring motion to an end, or plug it up – 让动着的止住，本义是把口堵上
column7: 停下：动着的东西不再动|停止：把「不再继续」用到行为与过程上|阻止：不让对方动起来，本义堵住正在这一层

column2: 中古英语 story ← 中世纪拉丁语 historia（叙事、饰带）← 希腊语 historia；中世纪教堂常在每层外墙做叙事饰带，遂以此指楼层
column3: one of the levels of a building
column5: The house has three storeys.|Her office is on the top storey.
column6: one horizontal level in a building's stack – 建筑上下叠起来的其中一层
column7: 层：上下相叠中的一个|楼层：连着楼房一起说，指第几层

column2: 中古英语 storm ← 古英语 storm（暴风、猛攻）← 原始日耳曼语 *sturmaz（风暴）← 原始印欧语 *(s)twerH-（搅动、驱赶）；与 stir 同源
column3: violent weather with strong wind and usually rain or snow
column5: The storm tore branches from the trees.|Troops stormed the castle gate.
column6: air thrown into violence that hits everything at once – 天气搅到发狂，一下扑到所有东西上
column7: 暴风雨：狂风加急雨的天气|风暴：不限雨雪，泛指这类猛烈天气|猛攻：把「一下扑上来」用到攻打上

column2: 中古英语 storie ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 estorie ← 拉丁语 historia ← 希腊语 historia（考究所得的学问）；与 history、storey 同源
column3: an account of events, real or made up, told in order
column5: She read the children a bedtime story.|The paper ran a story on the flood.
column6: events told one after another so they make a whole – 一件接一件讲下来，连成一整段
column7: 故事：讲出来的一段经历，真假不论|情节：这段经历里事件的先后与因果|报道：把真实之事按这种讲法写出来

column2: 借自中古荷兰语／中古低地德语 stove（暖房、浴室）← 原始西日耳曼语 *stubu（烧热的屋子），更早词源不明
column3: a piece of equipment that gives heat for cooking or for warming a room
column5: She put the kettle on the stove.|A wood stove heated the whole cabin.
column6: an enclosed fire that gives out steady heat – 把火围在里面，稳稳往外放热
column7: 炉子：烧火取暖或做饭的那件器具|火炉：偏重取暖那一用|灶：偏重做饭那一用

column2: 中古英语 streight，是 strecchen（拉伸）的过去分词 ← 古英语 streċċan（拉伸）← 原始西日耳曼语 *strakkjan（拉直）
column3: going in one direction without a bend or curve
column5: Draw a straight line down the page.|Give me a straight answer.
column6: pulled taut so no bend is left – 拉紧到一点弯都不剩
column7: 直的：形状上没有弯折|坦率的：话不绕弯，直接说到点上|连续的：中间不断开，如连赢三场

column2: 由 straight ＋ forward 复合而成；straight 一支 ← 古英语 streċċan（拉伸）的过去分词
column3: easy to understand or do, with nothing hidden or complicated
column4: 直截了当的/简单明了的
column5: The instructions were straightforward enough.|He gave a straightforward account of the night.
column6: going right ahead with nothing in the way – 一路朝前，中间不设弯绕
column7: 直截了当的：说话做事不铺垫、不迂回|简单明了的：事情本身没有复杂处，一看就懂

column2: 中古英语 straunge ← 古法语 estrange ← 拉丁语 extraneus（外面的）← extra（外部）
column3: unusual or unfamiliar in a way that is hard to explain
column4: 奇怪的/陌生的/不寻常的
column5: A strange noise came from the attic.|The town felt strange after ten years away.
column6: coming from outside what one knows – 来自自己所知之外
column7: 奇怪的：与常理不合，说不上来哪里不对|陌生的：不在自己熟悉的范围内|不寻常的：出现的频率与常态不符

column2: 中古英语 straunger ← 古法语 estrangier（外来的）← estrange ← 拉丁语 extraneus（外面的）← extra（外部）
column3: someone you do not know
column5: Do not open the door to strangers.|In this village a stranger is noticed at once.
column6: a person from outside the circle one knows – 自己所识之外的那个人
column7: 陌生人：没打过交道、认不出的人|外来者：来自本地之外的人，重点在来处

column2: 英语 strap 是 strope（挽具上的环）的变体 ← 古英语 stropp（带、皮条）与古法语 estrope ← 拉丁语 stroppus ← 希腊语 strophos（绳）← strepho（扭、拧）
column3: a narrow band of leather or cloth used to fasten or carry something
column5: The bag hung from a leather strap.|Strap the load down before you drive.
column6: a narrow band drawn tight to hold something in place – 收紧后把东西固定住的一条窄带
column7: 带子：狭长柔韧的一条|绑带：专用来收紧固定的那种|捆扎：把这条带收紧固定这个动作

column2: 源自拉丁语 strategia ← 希腊语 strategia（将帅之职、统帅术）← strategos（将军）← stratos（军队）＋ ago（率领）
column3: a general plan made to reach a goal over time
column5: The company changed its pricing strategy.|We need a strategy for the next election.
column6: a plan that decides the whole course before the moves – 先定下全局走法，再落每一步
column7: 战略：全局层面的长远打算|策略：为达成某事采用的具体路数|谋划：拟定这套打算这个过程

column2: 中古英语 straw ← 古英语 strēaw ← 原始日耳曼语 *strawą（撒开之物、秸秆）← 原始印欧语 *strew-（铺撒）
column3: the dried stalks of grain, or a thin tube for drinking
column5: The barn floor was covered with straw.|She drank the juice through a straw.
column6: a dry hollow stalk left after the grain is taken – 谷粒收走后剩下的那截干空茎
column7: 稻草：稻子脱粒后剩的干茎|麦秆：麦子脱粒后剩的干茎|吸管：形状与那截空茎一样，故借其名

column2: 中古英语 strawberie ← 古英语 strēawberġe，即 straw ＋ berry；得名或因野生植株靠草秆状匍匐茎蔓生，或因旧时采摘时把果子串在草秆上
column3: a small soft red fruit with tiny seeds on its surface
column5: We picked strawberries all morning.|She made a strawberry tart for dessert.
column6: a soft red fruit that carries its seeds outside – 红软的果子，籽长在外面

column2: 中古英语 streem ← 古英语 strēam ← 原始日耳曼语 *straumaz（水流）← 原始印欧语 *srew-（流动）
column3: a small narrow river, or a continuous flow of something
column5: A stream ran behind the cottage.|A stream of visitors arrived all afternoon.
column6: water moving steadily along one course – 顺着一条路不断流下去的水
column7: 小溪：窄而浅的活水|水流：流动着的那股水本身|一连串：把「不断流过」用到人或事上，接连不停

column2: 由 stream ＋ line 构成；stream 一支 ← 古英语 strēam（水流）← 原始日耳曼语 *straumaz
column3: to shape something so that it moves through air or water with least resistance, or to make a system simpler
column5: The new train has a streamlined nose.|They streamlined the approval process.
column6: shaped so that what flows past meets no obstruction – 削到让流过的东西碰不上阻挡
column7: 流线型：外形削得平顺，阻力最小|精简：把流程上多余的凸起去掉|使顺畅：去掉阻挡后，过程走得不再卡顿

column2: 中古英语 strete ← 古英语 strēt ← 晚期拉丁语 (via) strata（铺过的路）← sternō（铺开、摊开）；经原始西日耳曼语 *strātu 早期传入
column3: a public road in a town with buildings along it
column5: They live on a quiet street.|Cross the street at the lights.
column6: a paved way with buildings standing along both sides – 铺过的路，两侧立着房屋
column7: 街道：城镇中两侧有房的路|马路：同一条路，偏重供车通行那一面

column2: 中古英语 strengthe ← 古英语 strengþu ← 原始西日耳曼语 *strangiþu，即 strong ＋ 抽象名词后缀 -th
column3: the quality of being physically powerful or hard to break
column5: He lacked the strength to lift the crate.|Test the strength of the rope first.
column6: how much force something can put out or take – 能发出多大力，或能受住多大力
column7: 力量：能发出的力有多大|强度：能承住多少而不坏|长处：把「强的那一面」用到人的能力上

column2: 由 strength ＋ -en 构成；中古英语已有 strengthen（12 世纪），-en 原是不定式词尾，后被重解为使动后缀
column3: to make something stronger or more able to hold up
column5: Steel plates strengthened the old bridge.|Regular exercise strengthens the heart muscle.
column6: to add to what something can put out or take – 给它加上更多能发的力或能受的力
column7: 加强：从外面添上一层，使更能承受|增强：使原有的能力变大|巩固：把已得的稳住，不让退回去

column2: 源自拉丁语 strenuus（敏捷的、奋发的）
column3: needing great effort and energy
column5: Avoid strenuous exercise for a week.|They made strenuous efforts to reach an agreement.
column6: taking so much effort that it drains you – 费的力大到把人耗空
column7: 费力的：做起来耗力气|奋力的：把力气全使出来的那种|紧张的：耗得紧、松不下来

column2: 中古英语 stresse，截自 destresse ← 古法语 destrecier ← 拉丁语 distringō（拉扯开）；并与另一支 estrece（狭窄）← 拉丁语 strictus（窄的）合流
column3: the force pressing on something, or the strain a person feels under pressure
column5: The beam bent under the stress.|He has been under a lot of stress at work.
column6: a force bearing down that shows up as strain – 压上来的力，显出来就是受不住的样子
column7: 压力：物体或人身上承的那份力|重音：读音上加重的那一处，同是把力落上去|强调：把话里的力落在某一点上

column2: 中古英语 strecchen ← 古英语 streċċan（拉长、伸展）← 原始西日耳曼语 *strakkjan（拉紧）← 原始印欧语 *(s)treg-（僵、挺）
column3: to pull something so it becomes longer or wider
column5: She stretched her arms above her head.|The road stretches for twenty miles.
column6: to draw something out so it takes up more length – 把它抽长，占的长度变多
column7: 伸展：把肢体或物件抽长|展开：从收着的状态铺到更大范围|一段：抽长后所占的那一截，如一段路

column2: 中古英语 striden ← 古英语 strīdan（跨步）← 原始西日耳曼语 *strīdan ← 原始日耳曼语 *strīdaną
column3: to walk with long steps
column5: He strode across the room without a word.|The company has made great strides this year.
column6: walking with each step reaching further than usual – 每一步都比平常伸得远
column7: 大步走：步子拉得开，走得快|迈步：单看跨出去的那一步|进展：把「一步跨得远」用到事情的推进上

column2: 中古英语 strif ← 古法语 estrif ← estriver（争斗）← 法兰克语 *strīban（争）
column3: angry disagreement between people or groups
column5: Years of strife divided the two families.|The region has known little but strife.
column6: two sides pushing against each other without yielding – 两边互相顶着，谁也不退
column7: 争斗：双方动起手来相争|冲突：两边利益或主张顶上了|纷争：争的头绪多而乱，一时理不开

column2: 中古英语 stryken ← 古英语 strīcan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *strīkan ← 原始印欧语 *streyg-（抚、擦、压）
column3: to hit something with force
column5: The hammer struck the nail squarely.|Workers voted to strike for higher pay.
column6: to bring one thing hard against another – 让一物重重碰上另一物
column7: 打击：用力打上去|撞击：两物相碰的那一下|罢工：工人集体停手，如同对雇主打出的一击

column2: 由 strike ＋ -ing 构成，取「一下打中人眼」之意；strike 一支 ← 古英语 strīcan（抚、擦、击）
column3: so noticeable that it draws attention at once
column4: 醒目的/显著的/引人注目的
column5: She wore a striking red coat.|There is a striking difference between the two drafts.
column6: standing out so sharply that the eye is caught at once – 跳出来得厉害，眼睛一下就被抓住
column7: 醒目的：在周围里格外扎眼|显著的：差别或特点大到不容忽视|引人注目的：使旁人不由自主看过来
